## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Siṅgālajātaka* (Ja 152, also attested as *Sigālajātaka*) is a birth story preserved in the *Jātaka* section of the Pali canon [Catalog; Anandajoti 2010]. In modern presentation it is titled *The Jackal*  and rendered thematically by Anandajoti as *Acting without Consideration* [Anandajoti 2010]. According to its opening nidāna, the Buddha recounted this story while dwelling in his gabled chamber at Vesālī, occasioned by a barber of that city.

In the story of the past, a pack of lions seeks to avenge an insult committed against their sister; they rashly pounce upon what seems to be a jackal, but which is merely a reflection. All the lions perish as a result of their unreflective leap, save for the Bodhisatta, who correctly perceives the illusion [Anandajoti 2010].
